title: umbraflow-project.json
$comment: The one shape authority for umbraflow-project.json. The offline project kit and the runtime loader both compile these exact bytes out of the framework schema catalog, so no reader can accept a document another refuses; a second, narrower reader in either of them would be the weaker of two spellings and would decide. A deployment block IS its registration, stated as intent: it names files and declares its Tools, and the loader derives every digest from the bytes it read. No member the loader reads is a hash and no project author types one there. template_cuts is the single deliberate exception and states why in its own $comment: its sources are not files of this project, so a content address is the only name they have. Every path member is typed as a bare non-empty string and given its spelling rule by requireManifestSpelling in modules/deployment/source/deployment/project-directory.cpp, because that rule is task_platform::ConfinedRoot's own (confined-file.hpp:52-55). Stating it a second time as a regular expression would be two spellings of one thing. Everything declarative is INLINE: a deployment's Tools and its observed-instance identity schemas are stated here rather than named by path, so one document is the whole declaration and has one identity, one digest and one admission decision. The only paths that survive are assets -- Luau modules and resources -- which the framework delivers without ever reading their meaning.

runtime_artifact.$comment: A directory, not a file: the installer reads runtime-model.toml and runtime-artifact.manifest.json out of a root by those fixed names.

template_cuts.$comment: The Locator templates `project build` cuts for this project, and the one place a project author writes a hash. A cut names its sources by sha256 and by nothing else, because a source is a capture of a running target rather than a file of this project: it is not in the source tree, it is not in the release, and a path member would name a screenshot on whichever machine happened to take it. That is the whole point of the capability -- no repository need reference a screenshot path -- so the alternative is not a nicer spelling, it is the defect. The member is stated even when it is empty, on the same terms as resources, so that a project that cuts nothing says so rather than being read as one whose declaration went missing. Resolving a hash to bytes is deliberately not the kit's job and never becomes it: the corpus root arrives at `project build --frames-root PATH`, outside this document, which is why nothing here can name a directory. Declared at the root rather than inside a deployment because generated/templates/ is one flat namespace for the whole build -- generatedTemplates in modules/project/source/project/project-kit.cpp refuses a repeated template path across all of them -- and because no member of a cut names a deployment.

Sha256.$comment: A content address, lowercase hex with no prefix, spelled as every other published document under schema/ spells one. ContentHash::parse wants the canonical `sha256:` prefix and the reader adds it; carrying the prefix here would make the member disagree with every other digest a project or the framework writes down.

PixelRect.$comment: A region of a source image in that image's own pixels. The lower bound on width and height is PixelRect::create's own refusal of an empty rect, restated here so the document is refused where it is written rather than where it is used. There is no upper bound but the representable one: the real bound is the source's extent, which only the decoded image knows, and image::cutRgba8Template judges it there.

template.$comment: Where the cut lands under the build's generated/templates/ family. Relative and inside that family; normalizeTemplatePath states both refusals, because leaving the family is a property of the path once resolved rather than of its spelling.

source_sha256s.$comment: Every source the cut is taken from, in the order they compose. The first decides the colour plane and the whole list decides the alpha plane: a pixel is opaque only where every source agrees, so cutting one region from several captures is how a template stops carrying a background that moves. One source is legal and means a fully opaque template.

PluginAuthoring.$comment: Which of the two authoring paths wrote the Luau modules `tool_closure` names. `generated` is the declarative tier: the project kit produced the module from an umbraflow-declarative-workflow-tool/v1 declaration. `hand-written` is the exception: the author wrote the closure. The author states it because only the author knows it -- nothing in the module's bytes carries it, and a path convention would be a rule the kit knows and the loader cannot apply, which is how the two readers drift apart.

PluginJustification.$comment: Why this deployment writes its Luau closure by hand instead of a declarative-tools declaration: it must name the umbraflow-declarative-workflow-tool/v1 member or semantic that cannot express the behaviour. Required of a hand-written plugin and refused for a generated one, because demanding a reason from the declarative tier is demanding a false one. PRESENCE ONLY, over ASCII whitespace alone: the pattern refuses a value made of spaces, tabs, newlines, carriage returns, form feeds and vertical tabs, and accepts one made only of U+00A0 or any other non-ASCII space. No reader here judges whether the text is true, and no reader can; a justification that names the wrong member -- or that is a lone NO-BREAK SPACE -- is a review finding at plugin acceptance, not a refusal. See docs/pitfalls/checks-that-cannot-fail.md.

NamespacedName.$comment: The one spelling of a namespaced name, and therefore of a Tool name wherever one is written: this deployment's plugin_id, the `name` of each Tool it declares, and the `tool_name` of each binding. The namespace is its owner's registered namespace and the local name is what follows the dot that ends it, so the dot is required rather than optional: an unnamespaced name has no owner and there would be nothing for the ownership rule to check.

Identifier.$comment: OP:`Identifier`, byte for byte as schema/umbraflow-operator-v1.schema.json spells it. A capability name, a version, a UI action key and an effect scope kind are all this one shape.

tool_bindings.$comment: Which entry of this deployment's own module closure answers each Tool `tools` declares. It sits here, beside `tool_closure` and `tools`, because a binding is the JOIN of a contract name and a code entry and belongs beside both rather than inside either: putting it in a Tool entry would make the declaration a caller can be served carry dispatcher-only data, and putting it in `tool_closure` would make a contract name a property of the closure. The loader derives project_tool_bindings from it and from nothing else, sorted by tool name the way it sorts resources, so declaration order here is never consulted. The member is stated even when it is empty, on the same terms as resources: an empty array is the whole statement `this deployment binds no Tool to an entry`, which is what a project shipping no handler declares, and an absent member would be that statement spelled a second way.

tools.$comment: Every Tool this deployment declares, complete, inline. There is no Tool Catalog file and no catalog document: these entries ARE the declaration, their canonical bytes are what tool_catalog_hash digests, and every bound a call is judged against is declared here and nowhere else -- so a widened bound moves tool_catalog_hash and therefore project_registration_hash. The array may be empty, which is the whole statement `this deployment declares no Tool`, stated rather than left absent.

observed_instance_identity_schemas.$comment: The identity schema documents this deployment supplies for the observed instances it can publish, inline and named. `name` is the identity the framework keys the compiled authority on and the value an observation proposal's identity_schema_id carries; `schema` is the complete JSON Schema document that judges a semantic identity basis. Each schema is compiled on its own, so reuse inside one of them is JSON Schema's own $defs and there is no cross-schema indirection to resolve. The registration's observed_instance_identity_schema_hashes pins each by the sha256 of its exact canonical bytes, so the set the deployment supplies and the set the registration owns are one set: editing a schema moves project_registration_hash, and a validator for bytes the registration never pinned cannot be added. The member is stated even when it is empty, on the same terms as resources, so a project whose plugin observes nothing says so rather than being read as one whose declaration went missing.

resources.$comment: The opaque supply this deployment's program is compiled over. Resources stay file paths while everything declarative is inlined, because a resource is an asset rather than declarative material: the framework delivers it to a program that has no filesystem and never reads its meaning.

if.$comment: The direct-plugin tier's admission gate, stated where both readers reach it. The guard restates required so this decision does not depend on which keyword the evaluator visits first.

else.$comment: A generated adapter IS the declarative tier and has nothing to justify. The member is refused rather than ignored: a gate that accepted one here would be asking the declarative tier to invent a reason, which is the thing the justification exists to prevent.

Closure.$comment: The one closure a deployment ships: the module graph compiled on the scoped program type, exporting exactly the entry points its `tool_bindings` name. There is one slot because there is one program a Project runs; a project that binds no Tool ships this closure with an empty `exported_entry_points` and an empty `tool_bindings`, because explicit emptiness is a value.

exported_entry_points.$comment: What the authoring path observed this closure to export, stated by the author and never derived here. The loader may not compute it from tool_bindings, because the load-time cross-check would then compare the table with itself; and it may not run the module to observe it, because the bridge would then compare exports with exports. It names entry points only -- plugin_id is a field of every closure and is never listed -- so an empty array is the whole statement that this closure offers no entry point at all.

EntryPoint.$comment: One entry the deployment's module closure exports, by the name the module exports it under. The spelling is the derived registration's own root_name, restated here the way NamespacedName is: an entry name this loader would refuse after deriving a registration is refused where a project author writes it instead.

ToolBinding.$comment: One row of the join: the Tool, by the name `tools` declares it under, and the closure entry that answers a call of it. A handler and an automation entry are one mechanism and there is no discriminator here to tell them apart -- what makes an entry startable at the top of a run is that the actor is admitted to start it, which is an admission fact and not a schema field.

name.$comment: The identity the framework keys the compiled authority on. Its grammar is umbraflow-project-observation-proposal-v1.schema.json's identity_schema_id byte for byte, because the two are one string: what a deployment names a schema here is what an observation proposal names it by, and a document admitting a spelling the other refused would declare a schema no proposal could reach.

schema.$comment: A complete JSON Schema document, inline. It is judged as an object here and compiled by the deployment, which refuses any keyword this repository's evaluator does not implement -- at load, where the deployment builds its authorities, rather than years later when a basis reaches the hole.

ArgumentSchema.$comment: The Tool's flat input schema, stated inline and enforced by the framework. Reuse inside one schema is JSON Schema's own $defs; there is no cross-Tool indirection, and two Tools repeating a definition is the accepted price of having one spelling.

EffectBound.$comment: One entry of the complete set of OP:EffectEnvelope this Tool may propose. An empty set is a Tool that may propose none, which is the honest declaration for a read_only Tool. payload_schema_hash is a pinned identity and not a document this project supplies: the framework compares it with what a proposal carries and refuses a mismatch, which is what stops a plan widening a Tool's blast radius without moving tool_catalog_hash, and it never reads the payload's meaning.

Tool.$comment: One complete Tool declaration. Every member is mandatory: a Tool the framework admits is one whose whole contract was stated, and an optional member would be an absence the framework filled in on the Project's behalf.

name.$comment: The Tool's name, namespaced under the namespace this deployment's plugin_id registers. The dot is required so that the name has an owner at all; that the owner is this deployment is the loader's own admission rule, which no JSON Schema can state because it compares two members of one document.

ui_action_bounds.$comment: The complete set of OP:EffectivePlan allowed_ui_actions entries this Tool may propose.

name.$comment: The name a program addresses this resource by. It is the registration's own root_name grammar, so a name this loader would refuse after deriving a registration is refused where the author writes it instead.
